title: What Do You Say Next?
learning_goal: Identify and apply the therapeutic communication technique of seeking clarification in response to ambiguous nonverbal cues from a patient, distinguishing it from nontherapeutic responses such as providing false reassurance or changing the subject.
target_audience: Pre-licensure nursing students, first or second year
visual_style: 2D semi-flat limited animation. Characters have clean outlines, flat shading with subtle gradient, and muted clinical color palette. Emotional expression conveyed through head turns, eyebrow movement, hand gestures, and body weight shifts. Mouth movement suggests speech without precise phoneme sync. No realistic hair physics, no complex locomotion, no photorealistic textures. All scenes share the same hospital room interior.

characters.name: Maya
characters.role: Nursing student (player perspective stand-in / on-screen character)

appearance.hair: Dark brown, pulled back in a low bun, no loose strands
appearance.build: Average height, slim to medium build
appearance.uniform: Light blue scrub top and matching pants, white undershirt, hospital ID badge clipped to left chest
appearance.distinguishing_features: Small stud earrings, no visible jewelry otherwise

characters.name: Carl
characters.role: Patient, 58-year-old male, admitted for hypertension management

appearance.uniform: Standard hospital gown, light green with white print, white blanket pulled to waist, sitting upright in hospital bed
appearance.distinguishing_features: Reading glasses resting on the bedside table, slight stubble

characters.emotional_baseline: Subdued, guardedly cooperative, carrying unspoken tension

scenes.setting: Single-occupancy hospital room, daytime. Soft window light from the left. Bedside table with a water pitcher and glasses resting on it. Vitals monitor visible in background. Clean, quiet, no visitors present.
scenes.character_actions: Maya enters from the left carrying a small tablet, approaches Carl's bedside, makes eye contact, and gives a brief professional smile. Carl sits up in bed; he glances up when Maya enters but keeps his arms folded across his chest, jaw slightly tense, and his gaze drifts toward the window as he gives short answers.

camera.angle: Medium two-shot showing both characters, with closer framing on Carl during his responses.
camera.movement: Static. Both characters fully visible. No zooms or camera movement.
camera.lens_effect: Slightly warm, neutral depth. No dramatic focus pulls.

audio.sound_effects: Soft ambient hospital room tone. Faint monitor beep in background.
audio.ambience: Quiet hospital room. Occasional distant hallway sound, low and unobtrusive.

dialogue.line: Good morning, Carl. I'm Maya — I'll be working with your nurse today. Mind if I check in with you for a few minutes?

clips.character_actions: Maya enters from the left carrying her tablet, steps to Carl's bedside, and makes eye contact with a brief professional smile. As she speaks, she settles her weight at the bedside and shifts the tablet to one hand — a gesture still in motion as the clip ends. Carl glances up when Maya enters but his arms stay folded and his jaw stays slightly tight.

camera.angle: Medium two-shot, Maya entering from the left, both characters visible.
camera.lens_effect: Slightly warm, neutral depth. No dramatic focus pulls.

dialogue.line: How are you feeling this morning? Any pain or discomfort I should know about?

clips.character_actions: Carl gives a minimal nod and his gaze drifts back toward the window mid-nod — the nod still completing as Maya begins her question. Maya tilts her head slightly and holds her tablet loosely, weight shifting forward toward Carl as she finishes asking.

camera.angle: Closer framing on Carl during his response, then pull back to medium two-shot for Maya's question.
camera.lens_effect: Slightly warm, neutral depth. No dramatic focus pulls.

dialogue.line: Okay. The doctor mentioned she'll be by later to go over your results with you.

clips.character_actions: Carl's arms tighten slightly across his chest as he answers, his gaze pulling further toward the window. Maya holds a neutral expression and begins lifting her tablet to make a note — the tablet still rising as the clip ends, the note not yet written.

camera.angle: Closer framing on Carl's face and upper body during his answer, then back to medium two-shot.
camera.lens_effect: Slightly warm, neutral depth. No dramatic focus pulls.

clips.character_actions: Carl gives a short nod but his posture stays closed — arms folded, jaw tight. His gaze is still drifting toward the window as he finishes speaking, settling there in a held stare. Maya's tablet hand is lowering back to her side, eyes staying on Carl.

camera.angle: Closer framing on Carl showing his averted gaze and tense posture pulling toward the window.
camera.lens_effect: Slightly warm, neutral depth. No dramatic focus pulls.

scenes.setting: Same hospital room, continuous from Scene 1.
scenes.character_actions: Maya places a hand briefly near the bed rail and gives a reassuring smile, then turns toward the vitals monitor; Carl is propped up in bed.

camera.angle: Medium two-shot, then close on Carl's face to show the flattening of his expression.

audio.sound_effects: Blood pressure cuff inflating sound. Monitor beep continues softly.

dialogue.line: I'm sure it'll be fine — the team here is really good. Let me go ahead and get your vitals.

clips.character_actions: Maya places a hand briefly near the bed rail and gives a reassuring smile as she speaks. As she finishes her line, she is already turning toward the vitals monitor — the turn still in progress, her back not yet fully to Carl.

camera.angle: Medium two-shot, then slightly wider to show Maya beginning to turn toward the monitor.

clips.character_actions: Carl glances at Maya, nods once, and looks back at his hands — the nod still completing as his gaze drops. His expression flattens. The silence holds, closed and uncomfortable. Maya notes something on her tablet without looking up, pen still moving as the clip ends.

camera.angle: Close on Carl's face to show the flattening of his expression, then pull back slightly to two-shot.

scenes.setting: Same hospital room, continuous from Scene 1.
scenes.character_actions: Maya pauses, sets her tablet down on the bedside table, and shifts her posture to face Carl more directly — open stance, leaning slightly forward, maintaining eye contact. Carl looks up; there is a beat of silence, then his shoulders drop slightly and he unfolds his arms, his voice quieter. Maya listens without interrupting, gives a small nod, and leans in a little more, her expression calm and present. By the end, Carl is no longer looking at the window — he is engaged with Maya.

camera.angle: Medium two-shot, with closer framing on each character during dialogue to emphasize the shift in connection.
camera.lens_effect: Same warm neutral. Slightly brighter feel as the scene opens up emotionally.

audio.sound_effects: Soft ambient hospital room tone continues. No abrupt sound cues.
audio.ambience: Same quiet hospital room. Slightly warmer feel.

dialogue.line: Carl, I noticed you crossed your arms when I mentioned the doctor coming by. Is there something on your mind about that?

clips.character_actions: Maya pauses, sets her tablet on the bedside table, and shifts to face Carl more directly — the postural shift still completing as she begins speaking. She is leaning slightly forward, weight continuing to settle toward him, as her question finishes. Carl is looking up, registering the change in her posture.

camera.angle: Medium two-shot, slightly closer on Maya as she leans forward and asks.
camera.lens_effect: Same warm neutral. Slightly brighter feel as the scene opens up emotionally.

dialogue.line: I just... I don't know what she's going to tell me. I'm a little scared, honestly.

clips.character_actions: A beat of silence as Carl processes Maya's question. His shoulders begin to drop as he starts speaking — a slow exhale visible as the words come. His arms are unfolding mid-clip, still moving apart as he finishes his line. Maya listens without any expression that would interrupt him.

camera.angle: Closer framing on Carl to capture the emotional shift — shoulders dropping, arms unfolding mid-motion.
camera.lens_effect: Same warm neutral. Slightly brighter feel.

dialogue.line: That makes a lot of sense. It's okay to feel that way — and I'm glad you told me. We can talk through what to expect before she comes in.

clips.character_actions: Maya gives a small, genuine nod as Carl finishes. She is leaning in slightly more as she begins responding, her lean continuing to deepen through the clip. Carl's gaze is moving from his hands toward Maya's face — the turn of his head not yet complete at the end of the clip.

camera.angle: Medium two-shot, slightly closer on Maya as she responds, back to two-shot.
camera.lens_effect: Same warm neutral. Slightly brighter feel.

clips.character_actions: Carl's gaze has fully settled on Maya — no longer toward the window. His arms rest relaxed at his sides. As he speaks, a small exhale of relief is visible. Maya holds a calm, present expression. The quiet between them at the end of the clip is settled, not tense.

camera.angle: Two-shot showing both characters, Carl now fully forward-facing and engaged with Maya.
camera.lens_effect: Same warm neutral. Slightly brighter feel.

scenes.on_screen_text: Seeking clarification of nonverbal cues opens the door to honest communication — and better care.

decision_points.question_text: Carl says he's fine, but his arms are crossed, his jaw is tight, and his eyes drift to the window when you mention the doctor's visit. What do you do next?

choices.text: Name what you observed and ask Carl directly: "I noticed you crossed your arms when I mentioned the doctor — is there something on your mind?"
Reassure him that everything will be okay and move on to taking his vitals.
choices.misconception: Providing false reassurance ('I'm sure it'll be fine') is a nontherapeutic response that discourages further expression of feelings and closes off the patient's opportunity to share genuine concerns.

choices.text: The patient said he's fine, so move on — ask about his pain level and begin the physical assessment.
choices.misconception: Accepting a patient's verbal 'I'm fine' while ignoring contradicting nonverbal cues (crossed arms, averted gaze, tense posture) reflects passive listening rather than active listening, and fails to seek clarification of an ambiguous response.
